sections.heading: Graphs of Simple Trigonometric Functions
sections.html:
• sin⁡(x)=sin⁡(180∘−x)\sin{(x)} = \sin{(180^{{^\circ}} - x)}sin(x)=sin(180∘−x)

  • cos⁡(x)=cos⁡(360∘−x)\cos\left( x \right) = \cos{(360^{{^\circ}} - x)}cos(x)=cos(360∘−x)

  • Sine and cosine shifted by 90°

  • Sine has x-intercepts at multiples 180°, and cosine at (90° + multiples of 180°)

  • tan⁡(x)=tan⁡(180∘+x)\tan{(x)} = \tan{(180^{{^\circ}} + x)}tan(x)=tan(180∘+x)

  • Goes to infinity at 90°, 270°, 450°, …

  • The tan graph has asymptotes at 90, 270, 450

  • Has x-intercepts at multiples of 180°

sections.heading: Trigonometric Equations
sections.html:
• CAST diagram helps us to see in which quadrants the trig ratios are positive

Q.2cos⁡(x)+1=0 for 0≤x≤360\text{Q.} 2 \cos(x) + 1 = 0 \text{ for } 0 \leq x \leq 360Q.2cos(x)+1=0 for 0≤x≤360

Step 1: Isolate cos⁡(x)\cos(x)cos(x)

2cos⁡(x)+1=02 \cos(x) + 1 =02cos(x)+1=0

2cos⁡(x)=−12 \cos(x) = -12cos(x)=−1

cos⁡(x)=−12 \cos(x) = \frac{-1}{2}cos(x)=2−1​

Step 2: Find base angle

cos⁡(α)=12\cos( \alpha) = \frac{1}{2}cos(α)=21​ (Ignore negative sign for base angle)

α=cos⁡−1(12)\alpha = \cos^{-1} ( \frac{1}{2})α=cos−1(21​)

α=60\alpha = 60α=60

Step 3: Determine the quadrants where the angle can lie

Use CAST diagram to identify quadrants

Since cos⁡(x)\cos(x)cos(x) was negative, we look for quadrants where cosine is negative

The solutions must lie in Quadrants II and III.

Step 4: Form angles in those quadrants using the base angles

Quadrant II

x=180∘−αx = 180^{ \circ} - \alphax=180∘−α

x=180∘−60∘=120∘x = 180^{ \circ} - 60^{ \circ} = 120^{ \circ}x=180∘−60∘=120∘

Quadrant III

x=180∘+αx = 180^{ \circ} + \alphax=180∘+α

x=180∘+60∘=240∘x = 180^{ \circ} + 60^{ \circ} = 240^{ \circ}x=180∘+60∘=240∘

Final Answer: x=120∘,240∘\boxed{ x = 120^\circ , 240^\circ}x=120∘,240∘​
